doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Practicing and playing today
summary: He practices in spasms, driven by album projects, and plays sideman gigs in Portland.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Do you get much time to woodshed at the piano these days?

Well yeah I do. I don’t exactly woodshed. I don’t know, I go into spasms of, like for a few weeks or a few months I get interested in learning repertoire or making up a repertoire for myself. You know what spurs me to practice is if somebody wants me to make an album and I’ve got to come up with piano solos, like I did for this last Arbors album. I had to kind of get some stuff in shape. That spurs me to play. I do quite a bit of sideman playing, not quite a bit, but a couple times a week maybe I play in Portland.
I liked your interpretation of “Groovin’ High” on this CD.
Oh thank you. Yeah. I like that too. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
